metrics.recommendation: orb r0.75 (pipeline borderline sustainable) or r0.5 (firmly positive)

learned: All bench variants at full sizing (r1.25) are pipeline-negative — combine pass density can't replace busted XFA accounts fast enough. ORB at r0.75 is the only configuration with near-sustainable pipeline metrics (15 combine passes vs 14 XFA busts at h200) AND positive returns across all 5 non-holdout years; it also holds on the 2022 holdout (PF 1.15).

variant: ORB r0.75 -- 2022 holdout confirmatory
learned: ORB r0.75 holds positive edge in the 2022 holdout year (PF 1.15, +$5,551) despite the rate-hike/tech-crash regime. Combine pass rate drops from 52% to 25% in 2022, but the strategy stays profitable -- more robust to the low-price regime than the fixed-point iFVG filters.

variant: MFE/MAE dataset + be_trail_r=1.0 exit ladder (iFVG and ORB)
learned: be_trail_r=1.0 hurts the Combine objective on both iFVG and ORB (both metrics worse for both strategies). The mechanism kills 'two-thrust' winners: price crosses 1.0R favorable, stop moves to BE, price consolidates back to entry and stops out instead of running to target. The distributions of loser-MFE and winner-MAE overlap at 1.0R -- there is no clean separation threshold that saves losers without also killing winners.

variant: MFE/MAE excursion infrastructure
learned: Per-trade MFE/MAE now ships with every backtest run as r_mfe/r_mae fields on BacktestResult.trades. The be_trail_r mechanism is wired and default-off. Four analysis CSVs cover iFVG and ORB (clean: partial_r=0; deployed: partial_r=1.5) for future exit-mode research.

variant: two-phase pipeline: iFVG r1.25 (combine) + ORB r0.75 and ORB r1.0 (funded)
learned: The two-phase model (iFVG for Combine + ORB r1.0 for Funded) generates $393/month -- 18% more than the best sustainable single-phase option (ORB r0.75: $333/month) -- because iFVG's fast combine cycle (6.0 days/attempt, 28.6 days/funded account) lets the pipeline support a more aggressive funded config while remaining sustainable (1.26x ratio). The key variable is combine pass speed, not combine pass rate -- iFVG produces funded accounts in 28.6 trading days while ORB r0.75 takes 68.6 days, even though ORB has a higher per-attempt pass rate (52% vs 21%).

variant: ORB r2.5 + pdr_enabled (60-day median gate)
learned: The prior-day-range gate cuts ~50% of ORB trading days but leaves combine pass rate and PF completely unchanged (12/61, PF 1.10 both ways). Prior-day range as a pct-of-close does not predict ORB trade quality; the filter selects a random ~50% of days with equal win rate.

variant: ORB r2.5 + pdr_enabled (60-day median gate)

metrics.note: both runs include 2022 in 5yr equity; baseline comparison uses same full-5yr file

learned: PDR cuts ~50% of ORB volume for only +2.4% PF improvement. Funded net drops 61% ($63k vs $163k at h200) because fewer combine attempts mean fewer funded accounts. Both variants are pipeline-negative at risk 1.25; PDR makes the pipeline slower without improving quality. The '2024 PF 1.45 regime gate' finding was from the regime_switch engine (which gated entire-day strategy routing, not individual trade quality).

variant: ATR-normalized displacement: min_absolute_body_pct=0.000238, stop_buffer_pct=0.000143 (iFVG-only and combined)
learned: Loosening min_absolute_body from 5.0 to 3.9 pts at 16k NQ (pct=0.000238) generates 45 more displacement events per month in 2023-12 but leaves 2022-23 trade counts unchanged (same 2-18 per month). The 2022-23 drought is NOT caused by fixed-point threshold strictness -- it is structure-poverty (no iFVG setups, not filtered setups). The extra marginal displacements (bodies in 3.9-5.0 pt range) consume sweep states in the composer, slightly degrading high-quality months like 2021-11 (65->50 trades, PF 1.53->1.07). Feature shipped default-off; the infrastructure is sound but the hypothesis is wrong.

variant: kz_levels engine — KillzoneLevelTracker (London/NY AM/NY PM H/L sweeps), target_clarity_mode=off, risk 1.25%, 2 contracts, r2.0
learned: KZ session-level sweeps have identical edge quality to iFVG swing sweeps (PF 1.18 matches baseline) but ~10x lower trade frequency (~7.4/mo vs ~70/mo). 0/61 combine passes vs 13/61 (21%) baseline. The Combine requires throughput: 7 trades/month can't compound to $3,000 even at 60% WR. Root cause: session ranges lock once per session (London, NY AM, NY PM) and are first tested in the gap between sessions (e.g., London high at 05:15 ET, 3+ hours before NY AM opens). The sweep fires outside any trading window and was previously consumed silently; the fix keeps levels alive across the gap but the structural ceiling remains ~15 potential sweeps/week before the displacement filter. Two implementation bugs found: (1) dead-zone level consumption (fix: gate emit+consume on in_killzone()), (2) all_day() zone never closes (fix: kz_levels always uses default_killzones()).

variant: Session wk1-r1: ideation — MFE/MAE data mining + WebSearch

metrics.web_ideas_none_new: all web findings map to existing tested engines

learned: The iFVG short side is structurally loss-making on NQ 5min (PF 0.960 over 5y, 1251 trades); blocking shorts lifts long-only PF to 1.136 but cuts volume to ~25/month (funded route). ORB late breakouts (10:xx ET) have better PF than early ones (1.276 vs 1.176), supporting a 'reentry after stop' hypothesis; the current max_trades_per_day=2 is the wrong mechanism (fires before stop hits). External web research yielded no new engines — all practitioner ideas reduce to iFVG/ORB/KZ already tested.

variant: wall-clock flatten backup — flatten_wallclock_enabled flag + early-close calendar note
learned: The wall-clock backup task (_flatten_clock, every 30s) already existed and ran unconditionally in live mode — the B8 core fix was present. What was missing: a flatten_wallclock_enabled flag (now default True, preserving existing behavior), an early-close calendar note listing 8 known CME half-days for 2025-2026 in flatten.py, and two defining-behavior tests (clock-driven flatten without bar arrival, and flag=False gates task creation). The bar-driven path is insufficient alone: on CME early-close days bars stop at noon but the configured flatten time is 15:05 CT. The wall-clock covers this gap.

variant: ORB Rule-13 UI wiring — state() method + strategy_state SSE field + StrategyDebug panel
learned: All three Rule-13 layers implemented: (1) ORBDetector.on_bar logs when the OR range is first established after the window closes; (2) ORBDetector.state() returns {or_high, or_low, or_established, fired} — extracted from CombinedRunner.secondary in the strategy_state publisher in main.py, added as orb_state field in journal.publish_strategy_state; (3) StrategyDebug.tsx renders an ORB section showing the live range and signals-today count. or_established uses _or_range_logged (True only after first post-range bar) so the UI shows 'building...' during the 09:30+15min window and the confirmed range thereafter.

variant: exec_slippage column — fill vs order_bar_close (close of bar that triggered signal)
learned: exec_slippage = fill_price − order_bar_close (close of the confirmation bar when the signal fired) measures true execution quality: for market orders this is 0–2 ticks. The existing slippage column (fill − signal_entry, the FVG proximal edge) remains unchanged as 'plan_deviation' — it is still useful for diagnosing signal-to-fill price drift but not for execution quality. The watcher pattern (module-level _last_bar_close dict updated by an async on_bar handler registered in main.py) is the cleanest approach: no changes to Signal, no changes to strategy code, backward-compatible column ordering.

variant: long-only iFVG (allowed_sides=long) funded benchmark — r0.75/r1.0/r1.25
learned: Blocking short iFVG signals (PF 0.960, loss-making) via allowed_sides=long flips the standalone funded pipeline from pipeline-negative (sust 0.54x at r1.25) to self-sustaining (sust 1.13x at r1.25, 1.12x at r1.0). Both primary success criteria met: XFA net +41% ($186k vs $132k) and XFA busts -37% (53 vs 84). Trade volume cuts to ~65/month vs ~100/month full iFVG — the named-session killzones have a 65% long signal bias (vs 49.5% in all_day config), so long-only retains more volume than expected from the all-day MFE/MAE analysis. No new code needed: allowed_sides='long' already existed and is fully tested.

variant: ORB reentry after stop (orb_reentry_after_stop=True, r_multiple=2.5, risk 1.0%)
learned: ORB reentry after a confirmed stop adds +44% trade volume and improves combine throughput (7/61 → 11/61 at risk 1.0%) and funded net $/month (+35%). The cost is a -5% PF drop (1.213 → 1.153): reentry trades are lower-quality stop-reversal entries that drag average win quality down. Both standalone configs are pipeline-negative at risk 1.0% — the full value requires the two-phase model (iFVG combine + ORB funded). Mechanism implemented correctly: ORBComposer.on_stop_loss() re-arms detector exactly once per day via _rearm_count guard.
